topic: Filtering topic drift in multi-turn retrieval

selected_papers.title: DriftGuard: Detecting Topic Drift in Multi-Turn Retrieval
selected_papers.abstract: DriftGuard is a lightweight classifier that flags when a multi-turn conversation's retrieved passages have drifted from the conversation's original topic, filtering drifted passages out before they reach generation. On a multi-turn retrieval benchmark, DriftGuard improves retrieval precision over a baseline that re-retrieves without drift filtering. Evaluation is limited to English-language conversations.

executive_summary.content: DriftGuard addresses a specific failure mode in multi-turn retrieval-augmented generation: passages that were relevant to an earlier turn but have since drifted from the conversation's actual topic [1].

introduction_scope.content: Scope: this review covers exactly one paper, DriftGuard, chosen for its narrow, well-specified intervention point -- filtering retrieved passages by topical relevance to the current turn before generation. No broader survey of multi-turn retrieval is attempted.

thematic_findings.content: DriftGuard's contribution is specifically at the passage-selection boundary: it does not change how passages are retrieved, only whether an already-retrieved passage is allowed through to generation [1].

methodology_landscape.content: As a classifier applied after retrieval and before generation, DriftGuard is compositionally simple to reason about -- its own precision improvement is measured relative to a baseline that skips drift filtering entirely, not relative to a stronger retriever [1].

contradictions_open_debates.content: With only one paper in scope, there is no cross-paper contradiction to surface; the more relevant open question is internal to DriftGuard itself -- the paper does not report how filtering precision changes as conversations grow longer, which its abstract does not address [1].

gap_analysis.content: DriftGuard's evaluation is limited to English-language conversations, and the paper does not report results broken out by conversation length [1].

future_research_directions.content: A concrete next step is re-running DriftGuard's own evaluation broken out by conversation length, to test whether its reported precision improvement holds as drift has more opportunities to accumulate [1].

conclusion.content: DriftGuard is best read as a narrow, compositionally simple intervention at one specific point in a multi-turn retrieval pipeline, with its own evaluation scope-limited to English and to un-stratified conversation lengths [1].
